text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
-The government wants to impose a special tax on wastes both from households and industry. If the new tax is implemented, state income would increase by one billion crowns.
-It is more expensive to travel by bus and underground in Oslo than in most European cities. However the state transport company Oslo Sporveier still wants to raise ticket prices.
-Norwegian stae-owned oil company Statoil has bought American Blazer Energy Corporation for four billion crowns.
-Norway is climbing on a list over the world's most competitive countries. It is now considered to be the fifth most competitive country, while it was ranked in 10th place two years ago.

-Authorities in Chile disagree with Norwegian company Aker RGI's figures for how much it has invested in the country through its subsidiary Pesquera Yelcho. While Aker RGI says it has invested 140 million crowns, Chile says the investment is not larger than 28 million crowns.
-Norway-based SalOmega wants to conquer the U.S. health food market. Sixteen fish farmers who started the company say their fish are free of antibiotics and other chemicals.
-Aker RGI wants to sell 11.99 percent of its shares in Norway Seafoods.
-Aker Norwegian Contractors wants to take over the decommissioned offshore rig Brent Spar, cut it up and melt it into nails.
